t: Beginning with the reports required to be submitted by March 1, 2019, under section 1631 of the Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011 (Public Law 111–383; 10 U.S.C. 1561 note), information regarding a sexual assault committed by a member of the Armed Forces against the spouse or intimate partner of the member or another dependent of the member shall be included in such reports in addition to the annual Family Advocacy Program report. The information may be included as an annex to such reports.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a reporting requirement is a procedural interaction that counts as participation. It fails because this section only specifies the content of existing annual Defense Department reports on sexual assault, which stay inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, or member of the public is consulted or given a role in any federal decision, and no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: information regarding a sexual assault committed by a member of the Armed Forces against the spouse or intimate partner of the member or another dependent of the member shall be included in such reports

opus.w: This section only says what must go into existing reports under section 1631, which are prepared inside the Department of Defense and sent to Congress. Reporting to Congress stays inside the federal government. No state, expert, member of the public or other outside party is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. The procedural feel of 'reports' and the program name does not amount to outside participation.
opus.s: information regarding a sexual assault committed by a member of the Armed Forces against the spouse or intimate partner of the member or another dependent of the member shall be included in such reports in addition to the annual Family Advocacy Program report.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "reports" and the "Family Advocacy Program" suggest some formal process involving outside people. That reading fails. The reports under section 1631 are internal Department of Defense reports that end up with Congress. The section only adds a type of information to those reports and lets it go in an annex. No one outside the federal government is consulted before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates the inclusion of specific data in reports submitted to Congress. Since Congress is part of the federal government, this is an internal reporting requirement, not participation with outside entities. There is no consultation, hearing, or advisory role for non-federal parties involved in this decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Beginning with the reports required to be submitted by March 1, 2019, under section 1631 of the Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011 (Public Law 111–383; 10 U.S.C. 1561 note), information regarding a sexual assault committed by a member of the Armed Forces against the spouse or intimate partner of the member or another dependent of the member shall be included in such reports in addition to the annual Family Advocacy Program report.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that including information about sexual assaults in reports submitted to Congress constitutes "participation" because it involves sharing information with an external body. However, Congress is explicitly defined as being INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
